note: Planned compliance and legal framework packs. Editions are not pinned here; each pack pins its edition from the publisher when it is built.

groups.label: Security standards
groups.name: Security and secure-development standards
groups.text: Secure-development and security-management standards that customers and auditors ask for, built on the same scan evidence.

groups.label: Industry regulations
groups.name: Industry and sector regulations
groups.text: Sector rules for payments, healthcare, government, defense, medical devices, industrial systems, IoT and cars.

groups.label: EU regulation
groups.name: EU cyber and digital regulation
groups.text: EU laws for products with digital elements, essential services, the financial sector and AI systems.

groups.label: Privacy laws
groups.name: Privacy and data-protection laws
groups.text: Data-protection laws worldwide. They need the personal-data evidence planned in ROADMAP 5.2.4: where personal data flows, is stored and leaves.

groups.label: Middle East and North Africa
groups.name: Middle East and North Africa
groups.text: Cybersecurity and data-protection rules for Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt and the Gulf, after legal review, with Arabic and English reports.

frameworks.name: OWASP ASVS, Top 10, API Top 10, MASVS, GenAI LLM Top 10
frameworks.evidence: Built in: every finding maps through its CWE; the pivot for every other framework.

frameworks.name: NIST SSDF (SP 800-218)
frameworks.evidence: Secure code, review and testing (PW), vulnerability response (RV), SBOM and protecting the software (PS).

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A
frameworks.evidence: Secure development and coding, cryptography, logging, configuration, technical vulnerabilities.

frameworks.name: SOC 2 (AICPA Trust Services Criteria)
frameworks.evidence: Logical access, change management, vulnerability management and monitoring criteria.

frameworks.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
frameworks.evidence: Protect outcomes for data and platform security that code and config can show.

frameworks.name: CIS Controls
frameworks.evidence: Secure configuration, software inventory (SBOM), application security, data protection.

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-53
frameworks.evidence: Development (SA), integrity (SI), communications (SC), access, audit and configuration controls.

frameworks.name: CSA Cloud Controls Matrix
frameworks.evidence: Application security, cryptography, IAM and infrastructure controls; feeds CAIQ questionnaires.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27701, 27017, 27018
frameworks.evidence: Privacy and cloud extensions of ISO 27001.

frameworks.name: PCI DSS
frameworks.evidence: Secure software and public web apps (req. 6), card data at rest and in transit (3, 4), authentication (8), logging (10).

frameworks.name: HIPAA Security Rule
frameworks.evidence: Technical safeguards: access control, audit, integrity, authentication, transmission security.

frameworks.name: FedRAMP
frameworks.evidence: Through the NIST 800-53 pack, with an OSCAL export.

frameworks.name: CMMC and NIST SP 800-171
frameworks.evidence: Access control, audit, configuration, system and communications protection.

frameworks.name: HITRUST CSF
frameworks.evidence: Through mappings only; content needs a license.

frameworks.name: SWIFT Customer Security Controls Framework
frameworks.evidence: Secure software, credentials and logging on SWIFT-connected systems.

frameworks.name: FDA premarket cybersecurity (section 524B)
frameworks.evidence: SBOM, vulnerability handling and secure development evidence for medical devices.

frameworks.name: IEC 62443-4-1 and 4-2
frameworks.evidence: Secure development lifecycle and component requirements for industrial systems.

frameworks.name: ETSI EN 303 645
frameworks.evidence: Consumer IoT: no default passwords, secure updates, stored credentials, vulnerability disclosure.

frameworks.name: UNECE R155 / R156 and ISO/SAE 21434
frameworks.evidence: Automotive software update security and vulnerability management.

frameworks.name: Cyber Resilience Act
frameworks.evidence: No known exploitable vulnerabilities, secure defaults, SBOM, vulnerability handling.

frameworks.name: NIS2 Directive
frameworks.evidence: Article 21 measures: secure development, vulnerability handling, cryptography, access control.

frameworks.name: DORA
frameworks.evidence: ICT risk management for finance: secure development, testing, vulnerability management.

frameworks.name: EU AI Act
frameworks.evidence: Robustness and cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems; reuses the GenAI LLM Top 10 evidence.

frameworks.name: GDPR and UK GDPR
frameworks.evidence: Security of processing and data protection by design: personal-data flows, encryption, access.

frameworks.name: CCPA/CPRA and other US state privacy laws
frameworks.evidence: Personal-data flows to third parties, security of personal information.

frameworks.name: LGPD
frameworks.evidence: Security of personal data and data flows.

frameworks.name: PIPEDA
frameworks.evidence: Safeguards for personal information.

frameworks.name: DPDP Act
frameworks.evidence: Reasonable security safeguards for personal data.

frameworks.name: PDPA
frameworks.evidence: Protection obligation for personal data.

frameworks.name: APPI
frameworks.evidence: Security control measures for personal data.

frameworks.name: Privacy Act and Essential Eight
frameworks.evidence: Security of personal information; Essential Eight baseline controls.

frameworks.name: PIPL
frameworks.evidence: Security measures and cross-border data flows.

frameworks.name: POPIA, NDPA, Kenya DPA
frameworks.evidence: Security safeguards for personal data.

frameworks.name: Saudi NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC)
frameworks.evidence: Application security, cryptography, vulnerability and configuration management.

frameworks.name: Saudi NCA Cloud and Data Cybersecurity Controls
frameworks.evidence: Cloud configuration, data protection and data residency.

frameworks.name: SAMA Cyber Security Framework
frameworks.evidence: Secure development, application security and vulnerability management for financial institutions.

frameworks.name: Saudi Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL)
frameworks.evidence: Personal-data security and transfer outside the kingdom.

frameworks.name: UAE Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL)
frameworks.evidence: Personal-data security and cross-border transfer.

frameworks.name: UAE Information Assurance Regulation
frameworks.evidence: Technical controls for application security, access and monitoring.

frameworks.name: Dubai ISR and ADHICS
frameworks.evidence: Information security regulation for Dubai government and Abu Dhabi healthcare.

frameworks.name: Central Bank of the UAE requirements
frameworks.evidence: Technical controls for licensed financial institutions.

frameworks.name: Egypt Personal Data Protection Law (Law 151 of 2020)
frameworks.evidence: Personal-data security and transfer, with its executive regulations.

frameworks.name: Central Bank of Egypt cybersecurity requirements
frameworks.evidence: Technical controls for banks.

frameworks.name: Qatar PDPPL and National Information Assurance standard
frameworks.evidence: Personal-data security and information assurance controls.

frameworks.name: Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait and Jordan data protection laws
frameworks.evidence: Personal-data security.
